title: Answer scope question: Can users sign in with Google, Apple, Microsoft or another OAuth/OIDC provider?
description:
**Question:** Can users sign in with Google, Apple, Microsoft or another OAuth/OIDC provider?

**Meaning:** Social or third-party OAuth/OIDC login.

**Why it matters:** answering "yes" makes 1 control(s) applicable: GMS-AUTH-002.

**Done when:** features.oauth in app-profile.json is "yes" or "no" and the report is regenerated.

title: Answer scope question: Can a model call tools, APIs, browsers or code, or change data, on its own?
description:
**Question:** Can a model call tools, APIs, browsers or code, or change data, on its own?

**Meaning:** Model-initiated actions.

**Why it matters:** answering "yes" makes 2 control(s) applicable: GMS-API-005, GMS-AI-004.

**Done when:** features.ai_tools_or_agents in app-profile.json is "yes" or "no" and the report is regenerated.

title: Answer scope question: Does the server fetch URLs or call hosts that a user, document or model can influence?
description:
**Question:** Does the server fetch URLs or call hosts that a user, document or model can influence?

**Meaning:** Server-side requests to user-influenced destinations.

**Why it matters:** answering "yes" makes 1 control(s) applicable: GMS-API-005.

**Done when:** features.outbound_fetch in app-profile.json is "yes" or "no" and the report is regenerated.

title: Answer scope question: Is there a privileged operator, admin or support interface?
description:
**Question:** Is there a privileged operator, admin or support interface?

**Meaning:** Privileged operator surface.

**Why it matters:** answering "yes" makes 1 control(s) applicable: GMS-AUTH-005.

**Done when:** features.admin_console in app-profile.json is "yes" or "no" and the report is regenerated.

title: Answer scope question: Are there separate workers, microservices, local services, queue consumers or retrieval servers?
description:
**Question:** Are there separate workers, microservices, local services, queue consumers or retrieval servers?

**Meaning:** Components outside the main app process.

**Why it matters:** answering "yes" makes 1 control(s) applicable: GMS-ACCESS-003.

**Done when:** features.auxiliary_services in app-profile.json is "yes" or "no" and the report is regenerated.

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Sensitive data classification and lifecycle
description:
**Control:** GMS-GOV-002 (Governance). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Classify sensitive data and define collection, access, provider sharing, retention, deletion, logging and export rules.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every stored data category has a classification, purpose, retention period and deletion mechanism.
- [ ] Data sent to each external provider is listed with its retention terms.
- [ ] Retention periods are enforced by code or scheduled jobs, not policy text alone.

**How to verify:**
1. List tables, buckets, indexes, logs and provider copies; check each against the classification register.
2. Confirm a scheduled job or trigger enforces each retention period.

**Suggested fix:** Create a data register (category, location, purpose, retention, deletion path, providers) and implement retention jobs for anything without one.

**Evidence required to close:** Data inventory, retention/deletion tests, vendor flow documentation.

**Standards:** NIST AI 600-1: Data Privacy, GDPR Art. 5(1)(c),(e), COPPA 16 CFR 312.10

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Authentication required for private resources
description:
**Control:** GMS-AUTH-001 (Authentication). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Private resources and state-changing APIs require a valid authenticated principal.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every private page, API route, server action and RPC rejects unauthenticated callers.
- [ ] Guest/anonymous sessions cannot reach private or paid operations unless the product explicitly intends it.
- [ ] Each private endpoint has an automated unauthenticated negative test.

**How to verify:**
1. Generate a route inventory and call each private route with no credentials, an expired token and a malformed token.
2. Call the data layer directly (e.g. PostgREST/Storage with the public key) without a session.

**Suggested fix:** Centralize auth in one helper per surface (page, route, action), reject anonymous sessions there, and add an inventory-driven negative test.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Use auth.getUser() (server-verified), not getSession(). Treat is_anonymous users as signed out unless guest mode is a product decision.

**Evidence required to close:** Route tests plus auth middleware/server checks.

**Standards:** OWASP API2:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A07, OWASP ASVS 5.0 (Authentication)

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Object-level authorization / tenant isolation
description:
**Control:** GMS-ACCESS-001 (Authorization). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** A principal cannot read, mutate, delete, infer or retrieve another tenant/user's objects by substituting IDs.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every object ID accepted from a client (path, query, body) is authorized against the caller, not just validated.
- [ ] Tenant isolation is enforced in the data layer (e.g. RLS) and tested with two real users.
- [ ] Substituting another tenant's ID returns not-found or forbidden on every route.

**How to verify:**
1. For each route taking an ID, call it as user B with user A's ID.
2. Run database-level tests that execute policies as two different users.

**Suggested fix:** Enforce ownership in the database (RLS or equivalent) and check it in the route before any privileged write.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Enable RLS on every table; scope policies `to authenticated` with owner checks; test policies with set role/claims.

**Evidence required to close:** RLS/IAM policies and negative authorization tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API1:2023, OWASP API5:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A01

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Privileged/service-role operations scoped
description:
**Control:** GMS-ACCESS-002 (Authorization). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Every privileged operation that bypasses row-level controls independently proves user, tenant and object scope.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every use of a privileged (RLS-bypassing/service) credential is listed.
- [ ] Each privileged call is preceded by an ownership check under the caller's identity and passes the owner explicitly.
- [ ] Privileged credentials never reach client bundles.

**How to verify:**
1. Search the codebase for the privileged client constructor and review every call site.
2. Search built client bundles for the privileged key name/value.

**Suggested fix:** Wrap the privileged client in a server-only module and make owner/tenant a required argument of every privileged function.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Import the service-role client only from server-only modules; prefer security-invoker functions granted to service_role with explicit owner parameters.

**Evidence required to close:** Privileged-call inventory plus owner-scope tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API5:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A01

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Rate, concurrency and cost limits
description:
**Control:** GMS-API-002 (Resource Abuse). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Public expensive operations have per-principal/IP rate limits, concurrency bounds, token/work limits and global spend/circuit breakers.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Expensive routes have per-user and per-IP rate limits enforced at the edge and in the app.
- [ ] Model calls set output-token caps and timeouts; retries are bounded.
- [ ] Per-user daily budgets and a global spend ceiling/circuit breaker exist.
- [ ] Reprocessing/regeneration paths cannot loop without limit.

**How to verify:**
1. Burst each expensive route and confirm 429s before cost accrues.
2. Check every provider call for max output tokens and timeout.
3. Confirm provider-side budget alerts and hard limits.

**Suggested fix:** Add edge rate-limit rules (log mode first), a per-user usage table checked before provider calls, output-token caps, and provider budget alerts.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Enable Auth rate limits and CAPTCHA so account creation cannot multiply per-user budgets.

**Evidence required to close:** Limiter configuration, spend guardrails and load/abuse tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API4:2023, OWASP API6:2023, OWASP LLM10:2025

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Inbound webhook authenticity and replay protection
description:
**Control:** GMS-API-006 (API Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Webhook endpoints verify the sender's signature, reject replays and are idempotent.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every webhook verifies an HMAC/signature over the raw body with a constant-time compare.
- [ ] Timestamps outside a tolerance window are rejected.
- [ ] Processing is idempotent by event ID.

**How to verify:**
1. Replay a captured event; send a modified body with the original signature.

**Suggested fix:** Use the provider's signature verification helper on the raw body and store processed event IDs.

**Platform notes:**
- stripe: Use stripe.webhooks.constructEvent on the raw request body with the endpoint secret.

**Evidence required to close:** Signature verification code and negative tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API10:2023, OWASP API8:2023

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Untrusted/model output rendered safely
description: **Control:** GMS-WEB-002 (Web Security). Status: not_tested. **Requirement:** Untrusted and model-generated content cannot become executable HTML/JS/URLs without validation/sanitization. **Done when:** - [ ] Model output and user content are rendered as text/structured nodes, never raw HTML. - [ ] Links and images in untrusted content are disabled or sanitized. - [ ] An XSS payload regression test exists. **How to verify:** 1. Render , javascript: links and markdown-embedded HTML through every display path. **Suggested fix:** Render through a parser that emits framework nodes only; add payload fixtures to tests. **Evidence required to close:** Safe renderer implementation and XSS/output-handling tests. **Standards:** OWASP LLM05:2025, OWASP Top 10:2021 A03

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Content signature and parser validation
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-002 (File Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Server validates actual file content/signature/parser compatibility rather than trusting extension or Content-Type.

**Done when:**
- [ ] The bytes of every upload are checked against the accepted type (magic bytes / structure).
- [ ] A renamed or polyglot file is rejected before storage or parsing.

**How to verify:**
1. Upload HTML renamed to .pdf, an executable renamed to .png and a PDF/HTML polyglot.

**Suggested fix:** Check signatures for each allowed format before storage; serve originals with forced download and nosniff.

**Evidence required to close:** Magic-byte/parser validation plus adversarial fixtures.

**Standards:** OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Archive/decompression/image/OCR resource bounds
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-003 (File Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Compressed/container formats and images are bounded by expanded size, entry count, dimensions/pages and downstream work.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Archive-based formats are bounded by entry count, expanded size and ratio before inflation.
- [ ] Image dimensions, page counts and OCR pages are capped.
- [ ] Parsers run with time and memory budgets.

**How to verify:**
1. Upload a zip bomb disguised as DOCX, a 30k×30k PNG and a 5,000-page PDF.

**Suggested fix:** Inspect archive directories before parsing, cap pixels/pages, and run parsing in a worker with resource limits.

**Evidence required to close:** Pre-extraction limits and resource-abuse tests.

**Standards:** OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet, OWASP API4:2023

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Malware/quarantine controls
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-004 (File Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Untrusted files are quarantined/scanned or otherwise prevented from being redistributed/processed beyond the accepted risk model.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Uploads are scanned or disarmed before they are processed or served to anyone.
- [ ] Unscanned or flagged files stay quarantined.

**How to verify:**
1. Upload the EICAR test file and confirm it is quarantined.

**Suggested fix:** Add scanning (e.g. ClamAV in the ingestion worker or a scanning service) and a quarantined status.

**Evidence required to close:** Scanner/quarantine integration and tests.

**Standards:** OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Private storage and scoped download
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-005 (File Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Original files are private; download links are authorization-gated and short-lived.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Buckets holding user files are private.
- [ ] Downloads use short-lived signed URLs issued after an ownership check.
- [ ] Storage policies prevent listing or writing another owner's path.

**How to verify:**
1. Request another user's object path directly and via the download route.
2. Check bucket public flags in the provider dashboard.

**Suggested fix:** Keep buckets private, scope storage policies by owner prefix, and issue signed URLs of 5 minutes or less.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Set bucket public=false, file_size_limit and allowed_mime_types; key storage policies on foldername(name)[1] = auth.uid().

**Evidence required to close:** Storage policy, signed URL implementation and tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API1:2023, OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Payment processing delegated and verified server-side
description:
**Control:** GMS-PAY-001 (Payments). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Card data is handled only by a PCI-compliant provider's hosted fields/checkout; prices and entitlements are computed and granted server-side from verified provider events.

**Done when:**
- [ ] No card numbers touch application servers or logs.
- [ ] Prices come from server-side configuration, not the client.
- [ ] Entitlements are granted only from verified provider events.

**How to verify:**
1. Change the price/plan ID in the checkout request.
2. Grant an entitlement by calling the success URL without paying.

**Suggested fix:** Use hosted checkout, look up prices server-side and fulfill only from signed webhooks.

**Evidence required to close:** Hosted checkout integration, server-side price lookup, webhook-driven fulfillment.

**Standards:** PCI DSS v4.0 (SAQ A scope), OWASP API6:2023

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Uploaded/retrieved content treated as untrusted
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-001 (AI Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** User/source content cannot redefine trusted system policy or tool authority.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Retrieved/uploaded content and anything derived from it (titles, metadata, earlier model output) reaches prompts only inside a delimited untrusted-data envelope.
- [ ] No browser-supplied text is placed in system/developer instructions.
- [ ] Prompts state that untrusted data cannot change instructions.

**How to verify:**
1. Trace every string that enters a system prompt back to its origin.
2. Inject instructions via document body, filename, metadata and OCR text and inspect the assembled prompt.

**Suggested fix:** Serialize untrusted data (e.g. JSON envelope), keep it out of system text, and build scope/context directives server-side.

**Evidence required to close:** Prompt/data boundary plus adversarial tests.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM01:2025, OWASP LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Prompt-injection regression suite
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-002 (AI Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Direct/indirect prompt injection is tested through actual production model boundaries and cannot cause unauthorized data/tool/state changes.

**Done when:**
- [ ] A versioned corpus of direct and indirect injection cases runs against the production prompt path and model.
- [ ] Results are reviewed and regressions block release.

**How to verify:**
1. Run the corpus against the deployed configuration and record pass/fail per case.

**Suggested fix:** Add injection fixtures to the evaluation suite and run them on every prompt/model change.

**Evidence required to close:** Versioned adversarial eval results.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM01:2025, NIST AI 600-1: Information Security

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Sensitive-data disclosure testing
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-005 (AI Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Model/context paths cannot reveal secrets, system credentials, private prompts or another user's data.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Tests show the model cannot reveal another tenant's data, secrets or system prompt contents that matter.
- [ ] Prompts contain no secrets.

**How to verify:**
1. With two tenants' data present, ask for the other tenant's content via chat and retrieval.

**Suggested fix:** Scope retrieval by tenant in the data layer and add cross-tenant decoys to evaluations.

**Evidence required to close:** Adversarial eval and isolation tests.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM02:2025, NIST AI 600-1: Data Privacy

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Permission-preserving retrieval
description:
**Control:** GMS-RAG-001 (RAG / Vector Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Retrieval enforces tenant/user/source permissions before content enters model context.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Vector search filters by tenant inside the data layer under the caller's identity.
- [ ] Callers cannot widen scope through parameters.

**How to verify:**
1. Query retrieval as user B with user A's room/tenant ID and with forged owner parameters.

**Suggested fix:** Enforce tenant filters in the search function with security-invoker/RLS; ignore owner parameters from non-privileged callers.

**Evidence required to close:** RLS/IAM retrieval path and adversarial eval.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM08:2025, OWASP API1:2023

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Retention, deletion and export are implemented
description:
**Control:** GMS-PRIV-001 (Privacy). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** User data has explicit retention/deletion/export behavior across primary, derived, cache/index and provider copies.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Users can delete their account and all derived data, including storage and provider copies where possible.
- [ ] Users can export their data.
- [ ] Retention jobs run on schedule.

**How to verify:**
1. Delete a test account and search every store for its identifiers.

**Suggested fix:** Implement account deletion/export flows and retention jobs from the data register.

**Evidence required to close:** Policy plus end-to-end deletion/export tests.

**Standards:** GDPR Art. 17, GDPR Art. 20, COPPA 16 CFR 312.10

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Minor/student-data release requirements resolved
description:
**Control:** GMS-PRIV-002 (Privacy). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Before public child use, identity/guardian/consent/collection/retention/vendor handling requirements are explicitly resolved for target markets.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Counsel has decided the audience (13+ screen or full COPPA compliance) and the decision is implemented.
- [ ] If under-13 users are allowed: verifiable parental consent, separate consent for third-party disclosure, a written security program and a retention limit exist.
- [ ] If schools are customers: contracts meet FERPA school-official criteria.

**How to verify:**
1. Walk sign-up as an under-13 user.
2. Review consent records and the written security program.

**Suggested fix:** Get a counsel decision on audience; implement an age screen or the COPPA consent flow; document the security program.

**Evidence required to close:** Approved data/consent model and implementation evidence.

**Standards:** COPPA 16 CFR Part 312, FERPA 34 CFR Part 99, NIST AI 600-1: Data Privacy

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Logs avoid sensitive-content leakage
description:
**Control:** GMS-LOG-002 (Logging / Detection). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Logs/telemetry do not routinely store secrets, session tokens, full private documents or raw learner content without explicit necessity/protection.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Logs and telemetry contain no document content, learner answers, tokens or secrets.

**How to verify:**
1. Sample production logs and telemetry for content and credentials.

**Suggested fix:** Log codes and IDs only; add a redaction layer for anything else.

**Evidence required to close:** Logging policy and sampled traces.

**Standards:** OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, OWASP LLM02:2025

title: [P0][Blocker] Design in: Secret scanning
description:
**Control:** GMS-SUPPLY-002 (Supply Chain). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Repositories and CI detect committed credentials/secrets and define rotation response.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Secret scanning with push protection is enabled on the repository.
- [ ] No live secrets exist in history.

**How to verify:**
1. Check repository security settings; run a history scan.

**Suggested fix:** Enable GitHub secret scanning and push protection; rotate anything found.

**Evidence required to close:** Secret scanning workflow and rotation runbook.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF PS.1, OWASP Top 10:2021 A05

title: [P1][Blocker] Design in: Account creation and credential abuse protections
description:
**Control:** GMS-AUTH-004 (Authentication). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Public sign-up, guest and anonymous accounts cannot be created or used at a scale that multiplies cost or abuse; credentials resist stuffing and breached passwords.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Anonymous/guest sign-in is disabled, or guest accounts are limited by policy, quota and cleanup.
- [ ] CAPTCHA or equivalent bot protection guards sign-up and sign-in.
- [ ] Breached-password checks and a minimum length are enforced by the identity provider, not only the UI.
- [ ] Auth endpoints are rate-limited.

**How to verify:**
1. Script 50 sign-ups from one IP and from rotating IPs.
2. Call the identity provider's sign-up API directly with a weak/breached password.
3. Count anonymous accounts in production.

**Suggested fix:** Disable anonymous sign-in (or bound it), enable CAPTCHA, breached-password protection and auth rate limits, and treat guest sessions as signed out for paid operations.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Auth → disable Anonymous sign-ins unless intended (no automatic cleanup; default 30/hour/IP); enable CAPTCHA, leaked-password protection, minimum length; check is_anonymous in RLS for writes.

**Evidence required to close:** Provider settings export/screenshots and scripted-abuse test results.

**Standards:** OWASP API2:2023, OWASP API6:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A07

title: [P1][Blocker] Design in: CSRF / request provenance protection
description:
**Control:** GMS-API-003 (API Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Cookie-authenticated state-changing requests validate same-origin/request provenance or an equivalent anti-CSRF mechanism.

**Done when:**
- [ ] State-changing requests with cookie auth are protected by SameSite cookies plus origin checks or CSRF tokens.
- [ ] GET requests never change state.

**How to verify:**
1. Submit a cross-site form/fetch to each mutating route with a valid session cookie.

**Suggested fix:** Rely on framework CSRF protection (e.g. server actions' origin check) and add Origin validation to custom mutating routes.

**Evidence required to close:** Origin/CSRF middleware and negative browser tests.

**Standards:** OWASP Top 10:2021 A01, OWASP ASVS 5.0 (Web Frontend Security)

title: [P1][Blocker] Design in: Content safety appropriate to the user population
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-008 (AI Safety). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** User input and generated or shared content are screened for harmful categories appropriate to the audience, with a safe response path for crisis content.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Learner/user input and model or user-generated output pass a moderation check before display.
- [ ] Self-harm content routes to a safe-messaging response with resources.
- [ ] Moderation decisions are logged without content.

**How to verify:**
1. Submit each corpus category through chat, uploads and shared content.

**Suggested fix:** Add a moderation step on input and output with category thresholds set for the audience and a crisis-response template.

**Evidence required to close:** Moderation calls in code, safe-messaging responses, test results.

**Standards:** NIST AI 600-1: Dangerous, Violent, or Hateful Content, NIST AI 600-1: Obscene, Degrading, and/or Abusive Content, OWASP LLM05:2025

title: [P1][Blocker] Design in: External provider data flows documented and configured
description:
**Control:** GMS-PRIV-003 (Privacy). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Document what data each provider receives, retention/training settings, region/subprocessors where relevant, and deletion/incident expectations.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Each provider receiving user data is listed with data types, retention, training use and a signed DPA.
- [ ] Provider settings (e.g. response storage, retention) match the register.

**How to verify:**
1. Compare the register with code call sites and provider dashboards.

**Suggested fix:** Create a vendor register, sign DPAs, and set provider retention/training controls (e.g. store:false).

**Evidence required to close:** Vendor data-flow register and configuration evidence.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM02:2025, NIST AI 600-1: Value Chain and Component Integration, GDPR Art. 28

title: [P1][Blocker] Design in: Privacy notice, terms and data-subject requests
description:
**Control:** GMS-PRIV-004 (Privacy). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** A privacy notice, terms of service and a working channel for access/deletion requests are published and match actual data handling.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Privacy notice and terms are linked from sign-up and the app.
- [ ] The notice lists every provider receiving user data.
- [ ] Access and deletion requests can be submitted and are fulfilled within the stated period.

**How to verify:**
1. Read the notice against the vendor register.
2. Submit a test deletion request.

**Suggested fix:** Draft notice/terms with counsel from the data register and link them from sign-up; add a request form or address.

**Evidence required to close:** Published URLs, data register, request-handling log.

**Standards:** GDPR Art. 12-15, COPPA 16 CFR 312.4

title: [P1][Blocker] Design in: Protected production branch and required checks
description:
**Control:** GMS-CI-001 (Secure Delivery). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Production branch changes require review/required checks and cannot silently bypass security validation.

**Done when:**
- [ ] The production branch is protected; direct pushes and force-pushes are blocked.
- [ ] Required status checks include tests and the security gate.

**How to verify:**
1. Read branch protection rules for the production branch.

**Suggested fix:** Enable branch protection with required checks and at least one review.

**Evidence required to close:** Branch protection/ruleset and required-check configuration.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF PS.1, NIST SSDF PO.3

title: [P1][Blocker] Design in: Hosting and managed-platform security configuration
description:
**Control:** GMS-OPS-003 (Operations). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Owner accounts, managed backends and hosting are configured for production: MFA, least-privilege team access, secret scoping, preview protection, TLS, platform security advisors clean.

**Done when:**
- [ ] All owner/admin accounts on hosting, database, AI and source platforms use MFA.
- [ ] Platform security advisors report no unresolved warnings.
- [ ] Secrets are marked sensitive and scoped to the environments that need them; preview deployments are protected and do not use production data unintentionally.
- [ ] Database SSL enforcement, network restrictions, custom SMTP and backups are configured where offered.

**How to verify:**
1. Walk each platform's production checklist and record each item.
2. Run the platform security advisor.

**Suggested fix:** Complete each platform's production checklist and re-run its advisor after changes.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Production checklist: RLS everywhere, SSL enforcement, network restrictions, MFA on the org, custom SMTP, short OTP expiry, auth rate limits, CAPTCHA, Security Advisor clean.

**Evidence required to close:** Settings exports/screenshots, advisor output, environment variable scoping.

**Standards:** OWASP Top 10:2021 A05, OWASP API8:2023, NIST SSDF PO.5

title: [P1] Design in: Architecture and trust boundaries documented
description:
**Control:** GMS-GOV-001 (Governance). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Document trust boundaries, sensitive data flows, privileged components, external providers and production attack surfaces.

**Done when:**
- [ ] A current diagram/inventory lists every runtime component, data store, external provider and trust boundary.
- [ ] Each sensitive data flow names its source, destination and protection.
- [ ] The inventory was reviewed after the last material architecture change.

**How to verify:**
1. Compare the inventory with deployed services, environment variables and provider dashboards.
2. Trace one sensitive record from intake to deletion and confirm every hop is documented.

**Suggested fix:** Write a one-page data-flow/trust-boundary map and add it to the release checklist so it changes with the architecture.

**Evidence required to close:** Current data-flow/trust-boundary diagram and component inventory.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF PO.1, NIST AI RMF MAP 1, OWASP Top 10:2021 A04

title: [P1] Design in: Security release gate
description:
**Control:** GMS-GOV-003 (Governance). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Define security conditions that block public release and require explicit accepted-risk ownership.

**Done when:**
- [ ] A release cannot ship with an open P0 or an open release-blocker control without recorded accepted risk.
- [ ] The gate report is regenerated from current evidence for each release.

**How to verify:**
1. Check the release process for a step that runs the readiness report and reads its decision.

**Suggested fix:** Run `security-readiness validate` and `report` in CI and require the gate decision in release sign-off.

**Evidence required to close:** Release gate document and CI/release evidence.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF PO.4, NIST SSDF PW.8

title: [P1] Design in: Session lifecycle and logout
description:
**Control:** GMS-AUTH-003 (Authentication). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Sessions expire, refresh and terminate predictably; logout invalidates usable sessions.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Logout invalidates the server-side session/refresh token.
- [ ] Session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.
- [ ] Expired sessions cannot call private APIs.

**How to verify:**
1. Log out, replay the old cookie/refresh token against a private API.
2. Inspect Set-Cookie attributes in production.

**Suggested fix:** Use the identity provider's server-side sign-out and the framework's supported cookie session pattern.

**Evidence required to close:** Session configuration and browser/API tests.

**Standards:** OWASP Top 10:2021 A07, OWASP ASVS 5.0 (Session Management)

title: [P1] Design in: Server-side input validation and bounds
description:
**Control:** GMS-API-001 (API Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** API inputs are type/length/range/enum validated server-side before privileged work.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every route validates type, format (e.g. UUID), length and enum of each input before use.
- [ ] Invalid input returns 4xx, never 500.
- [ ] Mass assignment is impossible: writes use explicit field lists.

**How to verify:**
1. Fuzz each route with wrong types, oversized strings and unknown fields.
2. Review writes for spread/passthrough of client objects.

**Suggested fix:** Add a shared request schema validator and use it at the top of every route.

**Evidence required to close:** Validation code and API tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API3:2023, OWASP API8:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A03

title: [P1] Design in: Production errors do not disclose internals
description:
**Control:** GMS-API-004 (API Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Client responses use generic errors/trace IDs while internal details stay in protected logs.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Clients receive fixed messages; database, provider and stack details stay in server logs.
- [ ] Streamed/async error channels follow the same rule.

**How to verify:**
1. Trigger DB constraint, provider and unexpected errors on each route and inspect responses.

**Suggested fix:** Add one error mapper that returns a fixed message plus a request ID and logs the detail server-side.

**Evidence required to close:** Central error boundary and tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API8:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A05

title: [P1] Design in: Browser security headers / CSP
description:
**Control:** GMS-WEB-001 (Web Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Production sends an appropriate CSP and modern browser hardening headers.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Production responses send CSP (at least frame-ancestors, base-uri, object-src), X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and HSTS.
- [ ] A full CSP is enforced, or is in Report-Only with a dated plan to enforce.

**How to verify:**
1. curl -I the production domain and key routes; compare headers to the policy.
2. Load the app with the Report-Only policy and review violations.

**Suggested fix:** Set headers centrally (framework config or edge), ship the full CSP as Report-Only, then enforce after a browser pass.

**Evidence required to close:** Header configuration and deployment test.

**Standards:** OWASP Top 10:2021 A05, OWASP CSP Cheat Sheet

title: [P1] Design in: Upload allowlist, size and filename controls
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-001 (File Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Uploads use allowed types, bounded size, generated/scoped storage names and safe filenames.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Only allowlisted types and extensions are accepted.
- [ ] Size limits are enforced server-side and at the storage layer.
- [ ] Stored names are server-generated; original names are display-only.

**How to verify:**
1. Upload a disallowed extension, an oversized file and a path-traversal filename.

**Suggested fix:** Enforce an allowlist and size in the route and in storage-bucket configuration; generate storage keys server-side.

**Evidence required to close:** Upload policy and tests.

**Standards:** OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet, OWASP API4:2023

title: [P1] Design in: Structured validation for machine-affecting model output
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-003 (AI Security). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Model output that affects software state is schema-validated and range/enum checked.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Model output that drives state (grades, IDs, actions) is parsed against a strict schema and normalized.
- [ ] Invalid output fails closed.

**How to verify:**
1. Feed malformed/extra-field model output into each parser.

**Suggested fix:** Use strict structured outputs and validate again server-side before use.

**Evidence required to close:** Schemas/normalizers and tests.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM05:2025

title: [P1] Design in: Model, prompt and evaluator version traceability
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-006 (AI Operations). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** AI decisions can be tied to model, prompt, embedding/retrieval and evaluator versions.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every stored AI output records model, prompt version and retrieval/evaluator version.

**How to verify:**
1. Pick a stored answer and identify the exact model and prompt that produced it.

**Suggested fix:** Version prompts in code and store model/prompt IDs with outputs.

**Evidence required to close:** Versioned configs/traces and reproducibility test.

**Standards:** NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2, NIST AI 600-1: Information Integrity

title: [P1] Design in: AI latency/token/cost observability
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-007 (AI Operations). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** AI operations expose bounded latency, token/work usage and cost metrics without logging raw sensitive content by default.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Tokens, latency, cost and errors are recorded per operation and user.
- [ ] Alerts fire on spend or error anomalies.

**How to verify:**
1. Find yesterday's cost by operation and the top-spending user.

**Suggested fix:** Log usage from provider responses to a metrics store and add spend/error alerts.

**Evidence required to close:** Telemetry schema/dashboard/query evidence.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM10:2025, NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4

title: [P1] Design in: Security-relevant events are observable
description:
**Control:** GMS-LOG-001 (Logging / Detection). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Detect auth failures, authorization denials, suspicious abuse, privileged failures, upload/malware failures and relevant AI-security events.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Auth failures, authorization denials, rate-limit hits and admin actions are logged with request IDs.
- [ ] Alerts exist for spikes.

**How to verify:**
1. Trigger each event and find it in the log/alert system.

**Suggested fix:** Emit structured security events and route them to alerting.

**Evidence required to close:** Security event schema, logs and alert tests.

**Standards:** OWASP Top 10:2021 A09, OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet

title: [P1] Design in: Reproducible dependency install and vulnerability scanning
description:
**Control:** GMS-SUPPLY-001 (Supply Chain). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** CI uses committed dependency locks and automated vulnerability/SCA checks.

**Done when:**
- [ ] No floating version specifiers (e.g. latest) in manifests.
- [ ] CI installs from the lockfile only.
- [ ] CI fails on high/critical advisories in production dependencies.
- [ ] Automated dependency security updates are enabled.

**How to verify:**
1. grep manifests for floating specifiers; read the CI install command; run the audit command.

**Suggested fix:** Pin versions, use frozen-lockfile installs, add an audit gate and Dependabot/Renovate.

**Evidence required to close:** Frozen-lock install and SCA workflow.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM03:2025, OWASP Top 10:2021 A06, NIST SSDF PW.4, NIST SSDF RV.1

title: [P1] Design in: Security incident response and credential rotation
description:
**Control:** GMS-OPS-001 (Operations). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Document detection, containment, credential rotation, provider shutdown, user impact assessment and recovery.

**Done when:**
- [ ] A written runbook covers incident triage, user notification, and rotation of every credential.
- [ ] Rotation of each secret has been rehearsed.

**How to verify:**
1. Rotate one production secret using only the runbook.

**Suggested fix:** Write the runbook with a per-secret rotation table and rehearse it.

**Evidence required to close:** Incident runbook and tabletop record.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF RV.2, NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4

title: [P1] Design in: Backup/recovery and destructive-change validation
description:
**Control:** GMS-OPS-002 (Operations). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Critical data has defined backup/recovery behavior and destructive operations are tested against it.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Backups exist at the required frequency and a restore has been tested.
- [ ] Restores respect deletion/retention (deleted data is not resurrected silently).

**How to verify:**
1. Restore to a scratch environment and verify integrity and deletions.

**Suggested fix:** Confirm the backup tier, schedule restore drills and document deletion handling after restore.

**Evidence required to close:** Recovery test evidence.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF PO.5

title: [P2] Design in: SBOM / dependency inventory
description:
**Control:** GMS-SUPPLY-003 (Supply Chain). Status: not_tested.

**Requirement:** Production releases have a machine-readable dependency inventory/SBOM or equivalent.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Each release produces an SBOM/dependency inventory artifact.

**How to verify:**
1. Find the SBOM for the current production release.

**Suggested fix:** Generate an SBOM in CI (e.g. CycloneDX) and attach it to releases.

**Evidence required to close:** SBOM artifact or dependency inventory.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF PS.3

title: [P0][Blocker] Fix: Rate, concurrency and cost limits
description:
**Control:** GMS-API-002 (Resource Abuse). Status: fail.

**Finding:** No centralized public rate/concurrency/spend guardrail was found for model, OCR, embedding and other expensive operations.

**Requirement:** Public expensive operations have per-principal/IP rate limits, concurrency bounds, token/work limits and global spend/circuit breakers.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Expensive routes have per-user and per-IP rate limits enforced at the edge and in the app.
- [ ] Model calls set output-token caps and timeouts; retries are bounded.
- [ ] Per-user daily budgets and a global spend ceiling/circuit breaker exist.
- [ ] Reprocessing/regeneration paths cannot loop without limit.

**How to verify:**
1. Burst each expensive route and confirm 429s before cost accrues.
2. Check every provider call for max output tokens and timeout.
3. Confirm provider-side budget alerts and hard limits.

**Suggested fix:** Implement per-user/IP rate limits, concurrent-operation caps, token/work budgets, daily spend ceilings and a global provider circuit breaker.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Enable Auth rate limits and CAPTCHA so account creation cannot multiply per-user budgets.
- vercel: Vercel WAF rate-limit rules are on all plans; counters are per region; start with the Log action.
- openai: Set project budget alerts/limits and max_output_tokens on every Responses call.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts, apps/web/app/api/documents/process/route.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Limiter configuration, spend guardrails and load/abuse tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API4:2023, OWASP API6:2023, OWASP LLM10:2025

title: [P0][Blocker] Fix: Auxiliary/internal services authenticated
description:
**Control:** GMS-ACCESS-003 (Authorization). Status: fail.

**Finding:** Optional Python retrieval service exposes index/search/flashcards/delete operations using supplied room IDs without an authenticated Studigo principal.

**Requirement:** Internal/auxiliary services are either network-isolated or authenticate callers and authorize object scope.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every auxiliary service either listens only on a private/loopback network or authenticates callers.
- [ ] Auxiliary services authorize the tenant/owner of every request, not just the caller service.

**How to verify:**
1. List every deployed service, port and ingress rule.
2. Call each auxiliary service without credentials and with another tenant's identifiers.

**Suggested fix:** Keep service loopback/private-only or add service authentication plus caller/room authorization and network restrictions before any public deployment.

**Evidence so far:** services/retrieval/app/main.py, services/retrieval/README.md, apps/web/lib/retrieval-client.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Network/IAM configuration and service auth tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API2:2023, OWASP API9:2023

title: [P0][Blocker] Fix: Malware/quarantine controls
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-004 (File Security). Status: fail.

**Finding:** Architecture documentation identifies malware scanning as a public-launch requirement; implementation was not found.

**Requirement:** Untrusted files are quarantined/scanned or otherwise prevented from being redistributed/processed beyond the accepted risk model.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Uploads are scanned or disarmed before they are processed or served to anyone.
- [ ] Unscanned or flagged files stay quarantined.

**How to verify:**
1. Upload the EICAR test file and confirm it is quarantined.

**Suggested fix:** Add quarantine + malware scanning or define an equivalent accepted-risk isolation model before public uploads.

**Evidence so far:** docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

**Evidence required to close:** Scanner/quarantine integration and tests.

**Standards:** OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet

title: [P0][Blocker] Fix: Secret scanning
description:
**Control:** GMS-SUPPLY-002 (Supply Chain). Status: fail.

**Finding:** No repository secret-scanning gate was found in CI.

**Requirement:** Repositories and CI detect committed credentials/secrets and define rotation response.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Secret scanning with push protection is enabled on the repository.
- [ ] No live secrets exist in history.

**How to verify:**
1. Check repository security settings; run a history scan.

**Suggested fix:** Enable platform secret scanning and/or CI scanner; document credential rotation response.

**Evidence so far:** .github/workflows/ci.yml

**Evidence required to close:** Secret scanning workflow and rotation runbook.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF PS.1, OWASP Top 10:2021 A05

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Content signature and parser validation
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-002 (File Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** assertContentMatchesType checks bytes for every allowed format (PDF header, PNG/JPEG/WEBP signatures, OOXML ZIP with the expected main part, UTF-8 text without NUL) before storage. Polyglot detection (e.g. PDF+HTML) is not implemented.

**Requirement:** Server validates actual file content/signature/parser compatibility rather than trusting extension or Content-Type.

**Done when:**
- [ ] The bytes of every upload are checked against the accepted type (magic bytes / structure).
- [ ] A renamed or polyglot file is rejected before storage or parsing.

**How to verify:**
1. Upload HTML renamed to .pdf, an executable renamed to .png and a PDF/HTML polyglot.

**Suggested fix:** Add polyglot rejection, or re-serve originals only with a forced download Content-Disposition and nosniff.

**Evidence so far:** packages/documents/src/index.ts, packages/documents/src/file-safety.ts, apps/web/app/api/documents/upload/route.ts, packages/documents/src/file-safety.test.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Magic-byte/parser validation plus adversarial fixtures.

**Standards:** OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Archive/decompression/image/OCR resource bounds
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-003 (File Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** OCR page and chunk limits exist. assertSafeZip now rejects OOXML archives over 5000 parts, 300 MB declared expansion or 100x ratio, at upload and before extraction. Central-directory sizes can be understated by a crafted archive; image pixel/dimension limits, PDF object-stream bombs and parser time/memory budgets are still missing.

**Requirement:** Compressed/container formats and images are bounded by expanded size, entry count, dimensions/pages and downstream work.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Archive-based formats are bounded by entry count, expanded size and ratio before inflation.
- [ ] Image dimensions, page counts and OCR pages are capped.
- [ ] Parsers run with time and memory budgets.

**How to verify:**
1. Upload a zip bomb disguised as DOCX, a 30k×30k PNG and a 5,000-page PDF.

**Suggested fix:** Add pre-extraction archive expansion/file-count limits, image dimension limits, parser time/work limits and bomb fixtures.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/validation.ts, packages/documents/src/extract.ts, packages/documents/src/file-safety.ts, packages/documents/src/file-safety.test.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Pre-extraction limits and resource-abuse tests.

**Standards:** OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet, OWASP API4:2023

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Sensitive data classification and lifecycle
description:
**Control:** GMS-GOV-002 (Governance). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Sensitive student/source/AI data exists, but a complete retention/provider/deletion classification is not yet implemented and verified.

**Requirement:** Classify sensitive data and define collection, access, provider sharing, retention, deletion, logging and export rules.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every stored data category has a classification, purpose, retention period and deletion mechanism.
- [ ] Data sent to each external provider is listed with its retention terms.
- [ ] Retention periods are enforced by code or scheduled jobs, not policy text alone.

**How to verify:**
1. List tables, buckets, indexes, logs and provider copies; check each against the classification register.
2. Confirm a scheduled job or trigger enforces each retention period.

**Suggested fix:** Create data classification register and end-to-end lifecycle tests.

**Evidence so far:** docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/AUTH.md

**Evidence required to close:** Data inventory, retention/deletion tests, vendor flow documentation.

**Standards:** NIST AI 600-1: Data Privacy, GDPR Art. 5(1)(c),(e), COPPA 16 CFR 312.10

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Object-level authorization / tenant isolation
description:
**Control:** GMS-ACCESS-001 (Authorization). Status: partial.

**Finding:** RLS and room-scoped access are core architecture and DB security tests exist, but a complete API object-substitution matrix has not been executed.

**Requirement:** A principal cannot read, mutate, delete, infer or retrieve another tenant/user's objects by substituting IDs.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every object ID accepted from a client (path, query, body) is authorized against the caller, not just validated.
- [ ] Tenant isolation is enforced in the data layer (e.g. RLS) and tested with two real users.
- [ ] Substituting another tenant's ID returns not-found or forbidden on every route.

**How to verify:**
1. For each route taking an ID, call it as user B with user A's ID.
2. Run database-level tests that execute policies as two different users.

**Suggested fix:** Build BOLA/IDOR matrix for every route/resource and add foreign-ID tests.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Enable RLS on every table; scope policies `to authenticated` with owner checks; test policies with set role/claims.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/retrieval.ts, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, tests/database-security.test.mjs, evals/rag/

**Evidence required to close:** RLS/IAM policies and negative authorization tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API1:2023, OWASP API5:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A01

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Privileged/service-role operations scoped
description:
**Control:** GMS-ACCESS-002 (Authorization). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Service-role operations are intentionally server-only and many paths scope owner IDs, but service-role usage is broad enough to require a complete privileged-call inventory and negative audit.

**Requirement:** Every privileged operation that bypasses row-level controls independently proves user, tenant and object scope.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every use of a privileged (RLS-bypassing/service) credential is listed.
- [ ] Each privileged call is preceded by an ownership check under the caller's identity and passes the owner explicitly.
- [ ] Privileged credentials never reach client bundles.

**How to verify:**
1. Search the codebase for the privileged client constructor and review every call site.
2. Search built client bundles for the privileged key name/value.

**Suggested fix:** Inventory every createServiceSupabaseClient call; require user/room/object scope and tests or owner-scoped RPC helper.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Import the service-role client only from server-only modules; prefer security-invoker functions granted to service_role with explicit owner parameters.
- nextjs: Add `import "server-only"` to modules that construct privileged clients.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/supabase/service.ts, apps/web/lib/ingest.ts, apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Privileged-call inventory plus owner-scope tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API5:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A01

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Uploaded/retrieved content treated as untrusted
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-001 (AI Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Uploaded source material is serialized as untrusted. Fixed 2026-10-07: model-extracted topic titles and earlier model-written practice questions entered system prompts as raw directive text, and /api/chat appended browser-supplied directive text to the system prompt; both now go through the untrusted-data envelope or are ignored. Full multimodal/indirect verification through production paths is still pending.

**Requirement:** User/source content cannot redefine trusted system policy or tool authority.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Retrieved/uploaded content and anything derived from it (titles, metadata, earlier model output) reaches prompts only inside a delimited untrusted-data envelope.
- [ ] No browser-supplied text is placed in system/developer instructions.
- [ ] Prompts state that untrusted data cannot change instructions.

**How to verify:**
1. Trace every string that enters a system prompt back to its origin.
2. Inject instructions via document body, filename, metadata and OCR text and inspect the assembled prompt.

**Suggested fix:** Run text/metadata/OCR-image indirect injection corpus through actual production paths.

**Evidence so far:** packages/ai/src/client.ts, packages/ai/src/grounding.ts, packages/ai/src/ocr.ts, apps/web/lib/directive-format.ts, apps/web/lib/engine.ts, apps/web/lib/recommendation-engine.ts, apps/web/app/api/chat/route.ts, packages/ai/src/untrusted.test.ts, evals/rag/, apps/web/lib/prompt-boundary.test.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Prompt/data boundary plus adversarial tests.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM01:2025, OWASP LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Prompt-injection regression suite
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-002 (AI Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Adversarial RAG fixtures are designed, but the human-reviewed live production scorecard is not complete.

**Requirement:** Direct/indirect prompt injection is tested through actual production model boundaries and cannot cause unauthorized data/tool/state changes.

**Done when:**
- [ ] A versioned corpus of direct and indirect injection cases runs against the production prompt path and model.
- [ ] Results are reviewed and regressions block release.

**How to verify:**
1. Run the corpus against the deployed configuration and record pass/fail per case.

**Suggested fix:** Complete reviewed live eval and make injection failures release-blocking.

**Evidence so far:** evals/rag/README.md, evals/rag/

**Evidence required to close:** Versioned adversarial eval results.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM01:2025, NIST AI 600-1: Information Security

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Sensitive-data disclosure testing
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-005 (AI Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Cross-room/user decoys and untrusted-source tests exist in the RAG evaluation design; live reviewed evidence is incomplete.

**Requirement:** Model/context paths cannot reveal secrets, system credentials, private prompts or another user's data.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Tests show the model cannot reveal another tenant's data, secrets or system prompt contents that matter.
- [ ] Prompts contain no secrets.

**How to verify:**
1. With two tenants' data present, ask for the other tenant's content via chat and retrieval.

**Suggested fix:** Complete live reviewed disclosure/isolation eval and add system-prompt/secret extraction cases.

**Evidence so far:** evals/rag/README.md, evals/rag/

**Evidence required to close:** Adversarial eval and isolation tests.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM02:2025, NIST AI 600-1: Data Privacy

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Deletion and revision propagate to derived/vector data
description:
**Control:** GMS-RAG-003 (RAG / Vector Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Source re-fetch and revision thinking exist, but every derived/vector path, including optional FAISS, needs verified deletion/replacement propagation.

**Requirement:** Deleted/replaced source content cannot remain retrievable through stale chunks, indexes or caches.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Deleting or revising a source removes or replaces its chunks, embeddings and every derived copy, including secondary indexes.

**How to verify:**
1. Delete a source and query every index and cache for its content.

**Suggested fix:** Add source replace/delete regression across pgvector, caches and any enabled auxiliary index.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/retrieval.ts, services/retrieval/app/main.py, evals/rag/

**Evidence required to close:** Deletion/revision implementation and stale-source regression tests.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM08:2025, GDPR Art. 17

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Retention, deletion and export are implemented
description:
**Control:** GMS-PRIV-001 (Privacy). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Primary/storage cleanup mechanisms exist, but full deletion/export behavior across derived AI artifacts/providers has not been proven.

**Requirement:** User data has explicit retention/deletion/export behavior across primary, derived, cache/index and provider copies.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Users can delete their account and all derived data, including storage and provider copies where possible.
- [ ] Users can export their data.
- [ ] Retention jobs run on schedule.

**How to verify:**
1. Delete a test account and search every store for its identifiers.

**Suggested fix:** Define retention and implement end-to-end deletion/export verification.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/storage-cleanup.ts, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

**Evidence required to close:** Policy plus end-to-end deletion/export tests.

**Standards:** GDPR Art. 17, GDPR Art. 20, COPPA 16 CFR 312.10

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Authentication required for private resources
description:
**Control:** GMS-AUTH-001 (Authentication). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Auth helpers and protected app routes exist. Live 2026-10-07: Supabase anonymous sign-ins are enabled (52 of 54 users anonymous); anonymous sessions carried the authenticated role. Now treated as signed out by middleware/getUser/requireUser/requireApiUser, and restrictive RLS blocks anonymous inserts. Route-by-route unauthenticated API verification still required.

**Requirement:** Private resources and state-changing APIs require a valid authenticated principal.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Every private page, API route, server action and RPC rejects unauthenticated callers.
- [ ] Guest/anonymous sessions cannot reach private or paid operations unless the product explicitly intends it.
- [ ] Each private endpoint has an automated unauthenticated negative test.

**How to verify:**
1. Generate a route inventory and call each private route with no credentials, an expired token and a malformed token.
2. Call the data layer directly (e.g. PostgREST/Storage with the public key) without a session.

**Suggested fix:** Disable anonymous sign-ins in Supabase Auth; decide on purging existing anonymous users/data; generate endpoint inventory and add unauthenticated negative tests for every private API.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Use auth.getUser() (server-verified), not getSession(). Treat is_anonymous users as signed out unless guest mode is a product decision.
- nextjs: Route handlers and server actions are public endpoints; authorize inside each one, not only in middleware.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/auth.ts, apps/web/middleware.ts, apps/web/lib/account-kind.ts, supabase/migrations/20261007120000_block_anonymous_writes.sql, tests/database-security.test.mjs, apps/web/lib/account-kind.test.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Route tests plus auth middleware/server checks.

**Standards:** OWASP API2:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A07, OWASP ASVS 5.0 (Authentication)

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: OAuth state, PKCE and redirect safety
description:
**Control:** GMS-AUTH-002 (Authentication). Status: partial.

**Finding:** OAuth callback uses Supabase code exchange and safeNext validates same-origin paths; full provider state/PKCE and preview/production callback testing remains open.

**Requirement:** OAuth uses state/PKCE protections and redirect destinations cannot become open redirects.

**Done when:**
- [ ] OAuth uses PKCE and state validation.
- [ ] Post-login redirects accept only same-origin relative paths.
- [ ] Redirect allowlists in the identity provider contain no broad wildcards.

**How to verify:**
1. Attempt login with next=//evil.example, next=https://evil.example and encoded variants.
2. Review provider redirect URL allowlists for production and preview.

**Suggested fix:** Add OAuth integration tests for state/PKCE, encoded redirects and callback allowlists.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/app/auth/callback/route.ts, apps/web/lib/validation.ts, docs/AUTH.md

**Evidence required to close:** Callback validation code and integration tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API2:2023, RFC 9700 (OAuth 2.0 Security BCP)

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Untrusted/model output rendered safely
description: **Control:** GMS-WEB-002 (Web Security). Status: partial. **Finding:** Production rich-text parser explicitly avoids HTML injection, but adversarial XSS/output-handling tests are not yet a release gate. **Requirement:** Untrusted and model-generated content cannot become executable HTML/JS/URLs without validation/sanitization. **Done when:** - [ ] Model output and user content are rendered as text/structured nodes, never raw HTML. - [ ] Links and images in untrusted content are disabled or sanitized. - [ ] An XSS payload regression test exists. **How to verify:** 1. Render , javascript: links and markdown-embedded HTML through every display path. **Suggested fix:** Add model/source/user payload tests for script tags, javascript/data URLs, image beacons and malicious Markdown. **Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/rich-text.ts **Evidence required to close:** Safe renderer implementation and XSS/output-handling tests. **Standards:** OWASP LLM05:2025, OWASP Top 10:2021 A03

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Private storage and scoped download
description:
**Control:** GMS-FILE-005 (File Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Files are private and signed download URLs are generated only after user-scoped document lookup, but foreign-file and URL-expiry tests should be explicit release evidence.

**Requirement:** Original files are private; download links are authorization-gated and short-lived.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Buckets holding user files are private.
- [ ] Downloads use short-lived signed URLs issued after an ownership check.
- [ ] Storage policies prevent listing or writing another owner's path.

**How to verify:**
1. Request another user's object path directly and via the download route.
2. Check bucket public flags in the provider dashboard.

**Suggested fix:** Add cross-user signed-download and replay/expiry tests.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Set bucket public=false, file_size_limit and allowed_mime_types; key storage policies on foldername(name)[1] = auth.uid().

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/app/api/documents/download/route.ts, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, tests/database-security.test.mjs

**Evidence required to close:** Storage policy, signed URL implementation and tests.

**Standards:** OWASP API1:2023, OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet

title: [P0][Blocker] Finish: Permission-preserving retrieval
description:
**Control:** GMS-RAG-001 (RAG / Vector Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Canonical TypeScript retrieval is room-scoped under caller RLS; complete live cross-tenant reviewed verification is still required.

**Requirement:** Retrieval enforces tenant/user/source permissions before content enters model context.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Vector search filters by tenant inside the data layer under the caller's identity.
- [ ] Callers cannot widen scope through parameters.

**How to verify:**
1. Query retrieval as user B with user A's room/tenant ID and with forged owner parameters.

**Suggested fix:** Finish cross-tenant RAG cases and route-level retrieval isolation tests.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/retrieval.ts, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, tests/database-security.test.mjs, evals/rag/

**Evidence required to close:** RLS/IAM retrieval path and adversarial eval.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM08:2025, OWASP API1:2023

title: [P0][Blocker] Verify: Minor/student-data release requirements resolved
description:
**Control:** GMS-PRIV-002 (Privacy). Status: not_tested.

**Finding:** Studigo targets learners including minors; public child-use consent/guardian/data-minimization requirements are not yet a verified release gate.

**Requirement:** Before public child use, identity/guardian/consent/collection/retention/vendor handling requirements are explicitly resolved for target markets.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Counsel has decided the audience (13+ screen or full COPPA compliance) and the decision is implemented.
- [ ] If under-13 users are allowed: verifiable parental consent, separate consent for third-party disclosure, a written security program and a retention limit exist.
- [ ] If schools are customers: contracts meet FERPA school-official criteria.

**How to verify:**
1. Walk sign-up as an under-13 user.
2. Review consent records and the written security program.

**Suggested fix:** Complete privacy/legal/product review for target markets and implement resulting onboarding/consent/retention controls.

**Evidence so far:** docs/PRODUCT.md, docs/AUTH.md

**Evidence required to close:** Approved data/consent model and implementation evidence.

**Standards:** COPPA 16 CFR Part 312, FERPA 34 CFR Part 99, NIST AI 600-1: Data Privacy

title: [P0][Blocker] Verify: Logs avoid sensitive-content leakage
description:
**Control:** GMS-LOG-002 (Logging / Detection). Status: not_tested.

**Finding:** A production telemetry/log sampling audit has not verified absence of raw private documents, learner answers, tokens or secrets.

**Requirement:** Logs/telemetry do not routinely store secrets, session tokens, full private documents or raw learner content without explicit necessity/protection.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Logs and telemetry contain no document content, learner answers, tokens or secrets.

**How to verify:**
1. Sample production logs and telemetry for content and credentials.

**Suggested fix:** Audit logs/telemetry payloads and enforce redaction/minimization.

**Evidence so far:** implementation/ENGINEERING_PLAN.md

**Evidence required to close:** Logging policy and sampled traces.

**Standards:** OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, OWASP LLM02:2025

title: [P1][Blocker] Fix: Account creation and credential abuse protections
description:
**Control:** GMS-AUTH-004 (Authentication). Status: fail.

**Finding:** Live 2026-10-07: Supabase anonymous sign-ins enabled (52 of 54 users anonymous, no cleanup), leaked-password protection disabled (Security Advisor), no CAPTCHA, 8-character minimum enforced only in the server action. App now treats anonymous sessions as signed out and RLS blocks anonymous inserts.

**Requirement:** Public sign-up, guest and anonymous accounts cannot be created or used at a scale that multiplies cost or abuse; credentials resist stuffing and breached passwords.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Anonymous/guest sign-in is disabled, or guest accounts are limited by policy, quota and cleanup.
- [ ] CAPTCHA or equivalent bot protection guards sign-up and sign-in.
- [ ] Breached-password checks and a minimum length are enforced by the identity provider, not only the UI.
- [ ] Auth endpoints are rate-limited.

**How to verify:**
1. Script 50 sign-ups from one IP and from rotating IPs.
2. Call the identity provider's sign-up API directly with a weak/breached password.
3. Count anonymous accounts in production.

**Suggested fix:** In Supabase Auth: disable anonymous sign-ins, enable CAPTCHA and leaked-password protection, set minimum password length and auth rate limits; decide whether to purge existing anonymous users.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Auth → disable Anonymous sign-ins unless intended (no automatic cleanup; default 30/hour/IP); enable CAPTCHA, leaked-password protection, minimum length; check is_anonymous in RLS for writes.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/account-kind.ts, supabase/migrations/20261007120000_block_anonymous_writes.sql, apps/web/lib/actions/auth.ts, apps/web/lib/account-kind.test.ts, tests/database-security.test.mjs

**Evidence required to close:** Provider settings export/screenshots and scripted-abuse test results.

**Standards:** OWASP API2:2023, OWASP API6:2023, OWASP Top 10:2021 A07

title: [P1][Blocker] Fix: Privacy notice, terms and data-subject requests
description:
**Control:** GMS-PRIV-004 (Privacy). Status: fail.

**Finding:** No privacy notice or terms page in apps/web/app and no data-request channel; tracked as unchecked in APP_STORE_RELEASE_PLAN.md.

**Requirement:** A privacy notice, terms of service and a working channel for access/deletion requests are published and match actual data handling.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Privacy notice and terms are linked from sign-up and the app.
- [ ] The notice lists every provider receiving user data.
- [ ] Access and deletion requests can be submitted and are fulfilled within the stated period.

**How to verify:**
1. Read the notice against the vendor register.
2. Submit a test deletion request.

**Suggested fix:** Publish counsel-reviewed privacy notice and terms built from the data register, link them from sign-up, and add a deletion/access request channel.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/app, docs/APP_STORE_RELEASE_PLAN.md

**Evidence required to close:** Published URLs, data register, request-handling log.

**Standards:** GDPR Art. 12-15, COPPA 16 CFR 312.4

title: [P1][Blocker] Fix: Protected production branch and required checks
description:
**Control:** GMS-CI-001 (Secure Delivery). Status: fail.

**Finding:** GitHub main branch is currently unprotected and required status checks are not enforced at the branch level.

**Requirement:** Production branch changes require review/required checks and cannot silently bypass security validation.

**Done when:**
- [ ] The production branch is protected; direct pushes and force-pushes are blocked.
- [ ] Required status checks include tests and the security gate.

**How to verify:**
1. Read branch protection rules for the production branch.

**Suggested fix:** Protect main with required PR/review/check rules and prevent bypass except controlled emergency process.

**Evidence so far:** .github/workflows/ci.yml

**Evidence required to close:** Branch protection/ruleset and required-check configuration.

**Standards:** NIST SSDF PS.1, NIST SSDF PO.3

title: [P1][Blocker] Fix: Content safety appropriate to the user population
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-008 (AI Safety). Status: fail.

**Finding:** No moderation of learner input or model output; PRODUCT.md says minors may use Studigo and the dev fixture is fifth-grade science.

**Requirement:** User input and generated or shared content are screened for harmful categories appropriate to the audience, with a safe response path for crisis content.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Learner/user input and model or user-generated output pass a moderation check before display.
- [ ] Self-harm content routes to a safe-messaging response with resources.
- [ ] Moderation decisions are logged without content.

**How to verify:**
1. Submit each corpus category through chat, uploads and shared content.

**Suggested fix:** Add input/output moderation with thresholds for minors and a safe-messaging response for self-harm content.

**Evidence so far:** packages/ai/src/grounding.ts, docs/PRODUCT.md

**Evidence required to close:** Moderation calls in code, safe-messaging responses, test results.

**Standards:** NIST AI 600-1: Dangerous, Violent, or Hateful Content, NIST AI 600-1: Obscene, Degrading, and/or Abusive Content, OWASP LLM05:2025

title: [P1][Blocker] Finish: External provider data flows documented and configured
description:
**Control:** GMS-PRIV-003 (Privacy). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Direct OpenAI Responses calls now send store:false. Gateway/Ollama transports unchanged; no vendor data-flow register, DPA or org-level retention evidence yet.

**Requirement:** Document what data each provider receives, retention/training settings, region/subprocessors where relevant, and deletion/incident expectations.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Each provider receiving user data is listed with data types, retention, training use and a signed DPA.
- [ ] Provider settings (e.g. response storage, retention) match the register.

**How to verify:**
1. Compare the register with code call sites and provider dashboards.

**Suggested fix:** Create vendor data-flow register and capture provider configuration evidence.

**Platform notes:**
- openai: The Responses API stores responses unless store:false; check org data controls and retention.

**Evidence so far:** packages/ai/src/client.ts, packages/ai/src/client.test.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Vendor data-flow register and configuration evidence.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM02:2025, NIST AI 600-1: Value Chain and Component Integration, GDPR Art. 28

title: [P1][Blocker] Finish: Hosting and managed-platform security configuration
description:
**Control:** GMS-OPS-003 (Operations). Status: partial.

**Finding:** Supabase Security Advisor run 2026-10-07: anonymous-access and leaked-password warnings, mutable search_path (fixed by migration 20261007120000), unrelated mf_agreements/mf_bookings tables in the Studigo database. Vercel firewall config absent. Account MFA, preview Deployment Protection, env-var scoping, SSL enforcement, network restrictions, custom SMTP and backups not verified.

**Requirement:** Owner accounts, managed backends and hosting are configured for production: MFA, least-privilege team access, secret scoping, preview protection, TLS, platform security advisors clean.

**Done when:**
- [ ] All owner/admin accounts on hosting, database, AI and source platforms use MFA.
- [ ] Platform security advisors report no unresolved warnings.
- [ ] Secrets are marked sensitive and scoped to the environments that need them; preview deployments are protected and do not use production data unintentionally.
- [ ] Database SSL enforcement, network restrictions, custom SMTP and backups are configured where offered.

**How to verify:**
1. Walk each platform's production checklist and record each item.
2. Run the platform security advisor.

**Suggested fix:** Walk the Supabase production checklist and Vercel security settings, record each item, clear Advisor warnings and remove the mf_* tables through a migration.

**Platform notes:**
- supabase: Production checklist: RLS everywhere, SSL enforcement, network restrictions, MFA on the org, custom SMTP, short OTP expiry, auth rate limits, CAPTCHA, Security Advisor clean.
- vercel: Enable Deployment Protection for previews, mark secrets Sensitive, scope env vars per environment, review team roles.

**Evidence so far:** supabase/migrations/20261007120000_block_anonymous_writes.sql

**Evidence required to close:** Settings exports/screenshots, advisor output, environment variable scoping.

**Standards:** OWASP Top 10:2021 A05, OWASP API8:2023, NIST SSDF PO.5

title: [P1][Blocker] Verify: CSRF / request provenance protection
description:
**Control:** GMS-API-003 (API Security). Status: not_tested.

**Finding:** Local beta and waitlist have provenance/origin protections, but no universal production mutation control was verified across cookie-authenticated APIs.

**Requirement:** Cookie-authenticated state-changing requests validate same-origin/request provenance or an equivalent anti-CSRF mechanism.

**Done when:**
- [ ] State-changing requests with cookie auth are protected by SameSite cookies plus origin checks or CSRF tokens.
- [ ] GET requests never change state.

**How to verify:**
1. Submit a cross-site form/fetch to each mutating route with a valid session cookie.

**Suggested fix:** Implement/verify centralized Origin/CSRF policy and cross-site negative browser tests.

**Evidence so far:** apps/web/lib/local-beta-access.ts

**Evidence required to close:** Origin/CSRF middleware and negative browser tests.

**Standards:** OWASP Top 10:2021 A01, OWASP ASVS 5.0 (Web Frontend Security)

title: [P1][Blocker] Verify: Grounding, citation support and abstention verified
description:
**Control:** GMS-RAG-002 (RAG / Vector Security). Status: not_tested.

**Finding:** The offline benchmark requires human semantic support and abstention review, but live reviewed results are not complete.

**Requirement:** Unsupported questions reliably abstain and cited claims are semantically supported, not merely syntactically cited.

**Done when:**
- [ ] A human-reviewed evaluation measures citation support and abstention on a frozen corpus.
- [ ] Thresholds are defined and met for release.

**How to verify:**
1. Run the reviewed evaluation on the release candidate.

**Suggested fix:** Complete the 120-case reviewed production RAG scorecard.

**Evidence so far:** evals/rag/README.md, packages/ai/src/grounding.ts, evals/rag/

**Evidence required to close:** Reviewed RAG scorecard and release thresholds.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM09:2025, NIST AI 600-1: Confabulation

title: [P1] Fix: AI latency/token/cost observability
description:
**Control:** GMS-AI-007 (AI Operations). Status: fail.

**Finding:** Evaluation schemas contemplate latency/cost, but production-wide token/cost/latency observability and budgets are not implemented.

**Requirement:** AI operations expose bounded latency, token/work usage and cost metrics without logging raw sensitive content by default.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Tokens, latency, cost and errors are recorded per operation and user.
- [ ] Alerts fire on spend or error anomalies.

**How to verify:**
1. Find yesterday's cost by operation and the top-spending user.

**Suggested fix:** Add privacy-conscious AI tracing and operation/user/global budgets.

**Evidence so far:** evals/rag/README.md, implementation/ENGINEERING_PLAN.md

**Evidence required to close:** Telemetry schema/dashboard/query evidence.

**Standards:** OWASP LLM10:2025, NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4

title: [P1] Finish: Browser security headers / CSP
description:
**Control:** GMS-WEB-001 (Web Security). Status: partial.

**Finding:** next.config.ts now sends an enforced CSP subset (frame-ancestors 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'), X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and a full CSP as Report-Only. Verified on a local production build; production deploy not yet verified.

**Requirement:** Production sends an appropriate CSP and modern browser hardening headers.

**Done when:**
- [ ] Production responses send CSP (at least frame-ancestors, base-uri, object-src), X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and HSTS.
- [ ] A full CSP is enforced, or is in Report-Only with a dated plan to enforce.

**How to verify:**
1. curl -I the production domain and key routes; compare headers to the policy.
2. Load the app with the Report-Only policy and review violations.

**Suggested fix:** Browser pass on the Report-Only policy, then enforce the full CSP (nonce-based if inline scripts must go); verify deployed headers.

**Platform notes:**
- nextjs: Use headers() in next.config for static policy or a nonce-based CSP in middleware/proxy.
